privacy_intro: This page describes what this site does with personal data. Anyone can browse the museum guide without an account. An account is possible by invitation only.
privacy_collect: Without an account we ask nothing of you. We set no cookies, use no analytics or tracking and load nothing from third parties: your browser talks only to our own site. To limit abuse, a sign-up or sign-in request keeps the network prefix of your IP address (the IPv4 /24, or the IPv6 /56 and /48, never the whole address) and a check value (HMAC) of the email address, for at most two days. An unfinished sign-up keeps its email address, username and display name with the code for 24 hours.
privacy_accounts: You can create an account by invitation only. If you have an account, we store: your email address, your username, your display name, a hash of your password (only if you set one), the public key of each passkey you add, with its name, when you added and last used it and whether it is synced (no device or authenticator data; the passkey itself, its private key, stays on your device or in your password manager), hashes of your sessions, the invite you used, the time you confirmed that you are 16 or older and the version of the terms you agreed to. Codes we send by email are kept for 24 hours, only as an encrypted check value (HMAC). To limit abuse we keep, in time windows, only part of your IP address (its network prefix, not the whole address). The full IP address of an account sign-up and of a display-name change is kept for 30 days. We store no real name, date of birth or phone number and no tracking data. For your museum passport we store your visits (with an optional note only you can see) and your wishlist. We keep an import preview for 7 days, as parsed rows and not as the file itself. We keep an export for at most 7 days. Your visits, progress and wishlist are private by default and public only if you set them so; we then show a visit by month and only 24 hours after you log it. Your profile is not indexed by search engines unless you turn that on. In your account you can request an export of your data (JSON and CSV); we email you a link to your account page.
privacy_cookie: When you sign in we set one strictly necessary cookie, __Host-mjk_sid. It holds your session and applies to our own site only, not to our media server. It is kept at most 180 days; signing out ends the session at once. We use no other cookies. Once you sign in, your browser also keeps a small “signed in” marker in its local storage (localStorage), only to show your own visits and wishlist on the public pages. It holds nothing about you and is sent nowhere.
privacy_location: The “Museums near me” button sends your browser’s position to us only when you press it, rounded to about 100 metres, to find the nearest museums. We do not store or log it. Like every other request, it reaches us through Cloudflare.
privacy_logs: Our servers log fixed codes only (which kind of page, which status), no IP addresses, no email addresses and no search terms.
privacy_cloudflare: Every request passes through Cloudflare, which relays and protects the traffic. Cloudflare is a US company and our processor; it relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for the transfer. In doing so it processes technical data such as your IP address.
privacy_mail: We send codes, invites and notices about your account (an email change, a newly added passkey) by email through Lettermint, an email service in the Netherlands (EU). Lettermint is our processor and processes your email address for this.
privacy_backups: We back up the database every night. It also holds the account data (see “Accounts”). We keep the daily backups of the last 28 days. Older ones are deleted once a week, so no backup is kept longer than about 35 days.
privacy_lost: If you lose access to your mailbox, you can only still sign in with a password or a passkey, if you set one, and change your email address with it. Without either there is no recovery: the owner never moves an account on request.
privacy_rights: You may ask for access to, correction or erasure of data about you, object to a processing and have data transferred. Email us through the contact page. You can also complain to the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).

review_head_description: What members think of {name}: ratings and reviews from people who have been there.
howcheck_draft: This is a draft text, until the owner approves it.
howcheck_intro: Ratings and reviews come from members. This is how we handle them.
howcheck_visits: A member can only rate a museum for which they have logged a visit. The member declares that visit themselves: we do not check that they were really there. So it is a threshold, not proof.
howcheck_h_once: One review per member per museum
howcheck_once: A member writes one review per museum and can edit or delete it later. The date of the visit and, if there is one, the date of the edit are shown with the review.
howcheck_mean: A museum's score is the mean of all its ratings (1 to 5 stars), rounded to one decimal.
howcheck_aspects: We show an aspect (collection, presentation, kid-friendly, accessibility, facilities, value for money) only from 3 ratings of that aspect. Below that it says "too few ratings".
howcheck_rank: In the list, museums with a higher score come first. A museum with only one or two ratings should not weigh as much as one with a hundred. So we use a weighted mean:
howcheck_rank_why: Here n is the museum's number of ratings, Σ their sum, m the mean of all ratings of all museums and C = 5, the weight of that mean. With few ratings a museum stays close to m; with many ratings its own mean counts.
howcheck_negative: We never hide or demote a review because it is negative. A museum cannot ask us to remove a bad review.
howcheck_moderation: We only remove reviews that contain illegal content or breach the terms. A removed review no longer counts towards the score.
howcheck_staff: Reviews by staff or clients of a museum, and reviews written for a reward, are not allowed.
howcheck_report: Do you think a review is illegal or breaches the terms? Report it through the page
